title: A CXL Memory Rack for Multi-Turn LLM Serving
event_hint: HyMCache: CXL-hybrid memory rack for multi-turn LLM KV-cache serving
problem: Multi-turn LLM serving requires TB-scale shared KV-cache capacity to reuse context across turns and sessions, but GPU HBM and host DRAM are too costly to scale to this level. Storage-backed tiers provide capacity but require software staging overhead. Pure DRAM-based CXL memory pools provide low latency but remain expensive at multi-TB scale.
mechanism: HyMCache builds a remote memory rack using CXL-hybrid memory (CXL-HM), which combines small in-device DRAM with large SSD-backed capacity behind a CXL.mem interface. It exploits read-dominant, predictable, and append-only KV-cache access patterns with request-level prefix prefetching and opportunistic write buffering to stage latency-critical reads in device DRAM, enabling DRAM-scale efficiency at SSD-level cost.

evaluation_context: Real CXL-HM prototype evaluation under two configurations: (1) single-aggregator serving, and (2) Prefill-Decode (PD) disaggregated serving with 64 GB per worker (256 GB total). Uses RDMA-capable network (100-400 Gbps) for remote memory access. Leverages vLLM serving engine with PagedAttention and Dynamo distributed framework with NIXL for P-D KV transfer.
limitations: Evidence pack covers only abstract/intro/background; exact workload details, model specifications, dataset characteristics, request traces, and full evaluation metrics are in unread sections. Performance claims in abstract (3.0x, 1.45x, 30% gap) lack concrete baseline conditions and metric definitions visible in this excerpt. Cost estimates are rough projections for FPGA prototypes, not production pricing. CXL-HM internal cache management policies (beyond LRU being insufficient) are not detailed in visible text.
project_relevance: This source addresses KV-cache memory tiering for multi-turn LLM serving, which is highly relevant to cross-region cache sharing questions. The CXL-HM approach explores remote memory access over RDMA networks, which directly relates to WAN RTT and bandwidth considerations for KV cache transport. The 16x DRAM reduction versus 30% performance trade-off quantifies a key cost-performance decision point relevant to cross-region cache economics. Request-level prefix prefetching for predictable, append-only access patterns could inform compression and prefill strategies for cross-domain transfer. However, this paper focuses on intra-datacenter CXL/RDMA memory tiers rather than true WAN cross-region deployment; actual cross-region WAN latency (tens of ms) would be orders of magnitude higher than the CXL/RDMA latencies discussed (600-750 ns for switch fabrics).

evidence_gaps.question: What are the exact baseline LMCache configuration, workload characteristics (model, dataset, trace), and specific performance metrics (TTFT, TTFT, throughput, P99 latency) that support the 3.0x and 1.45x claims?
What is the detailed comparison methodology and absolute performance numbers for the 1TB Mooncake baseline that results in the ~30% performance gap claim?
What are the actual RDMA network characteristics (RTT, bandwidth utilization, queue depths) and their impact on end-to-end serving latency?
